body.text: Rugby League World Cup live: Kalyn Ponga returns for Kiwis against Tonga — blog and scores
New Zealand's bid to reach the men's Rugby League World Cup semifinal has been boosted by the return of fullback Kalyn Ponga, just 23 days after breaking his arm in the tournament opener.
Meanwhile, New Zealand's women are trying to make a seventh-consecutive final, facing Fetu Samoa in their maiden World Cup semifinal.
Follow the live blog below and tune in to our live radio coverage.

FULL-TIME: New Zealand 32 def. Fetu Samoa 0
New Zealand has secured its place in a seventh consecutive women's Rugby League World Cup final after beating Fetu Samoa 32-0.
Having made the decider in all six previous tournaments, flyer Stacey Waaka scored three tries to guide her nation to semifinal triumph.
New Zealand will face either Australia or Fiji, who play the second semifinal in Sydney on Sunday.
67' TRY: Raecene McGregor (7) scores for New Zealand
The scoreline is starting to get out of hand.
The Kiwi Ferns again roll down the field, picking apart a very tired Fetu Samoa defence.
Captain Raecene McGregor has scored under the posts.
64' TRY: Stacey Waaka (4) scores a hat-trick
Oh. What a pass from Annessa Biddle.
The Kiwi Ferns were keeping the ball alive near the Fetu Samoa goal-line.
Interchange Annessa Biddle leaps over a downed defender and, while in the air, throws a one-handed flick pass to Stacey Waaka, who scores a third try.
60' TRY: Kaiyah Atai (12) scores for New Zealand
New Zealand have marched down the field and scored a fourth try.
Quick play-the-balls allowed the Kiwi Ferns to roll down the field, with Fetu Samoa's defence in retreat.
Kaiyah Atai charged onto a short pass with defenders back-pedalling, and Atai muscled her way to the goal-line.
That's it — lay-down misère. New Zealand are going to win.
58' TRY: Mele Hufanga (3) scores for New Zealand
The Kiwi Ferns had a goal-line dropout, which was dropped over the sideline by Samoan halfback Pauline Piliae-Rasabale.
That took the air out of this match, as it felt like Samoa's chances were running out.
The Kiwi Ferns, aided by a penalty, marched down the field.
Destructive centre Mele Hufanga got the ball near the goal-line and shrugged off three defenders to score.
52' Alexis Tauaneai drops the ball with the line begging
The match could have been sealed for the Kiwi Ferns.
Ashleigh Quinlan made the linebreak near the goal-line, and as she was being tackled, passed inside to Alexis Tauaneai.
But Tauaneai could not hold onto the footy, and a certain try goes begging.
50' Fetu Samoa throws fourth forward pass as rain falls
Fetu Samoa has been its own worst enemy.
With the ball at halfway line, halfback Pauline Piliae-Rasabale tried to throw a cut-out pass to an open winger, but it went forward.
That is Fetu Samoa's fourth forward pass in this match.
44' TRY: Stacey Waaka (4) scores for New Zealand
Excellent from New Zealand.
The play started with the Kiwi Ferns shifting to the left, then they passed back to the right.
Raecene McGregor put in a perfect little kick that was caught by a charging Stacey Waaka, who scored.
Kalyn Ponga to start for Kiwis against Tonga
We have HUGE news from the New Zealand Kiwis.
Kalyn Ponga will start at fullback in tonight's semifinal against Tonga.
Ponga broke his arm in the opening match of the tournament against Australia — 23 days ago.
Second half begins between New Zealand and Fetu Samoa
New Zealand, holding an eight-point lead, has the first use of the ball in the second half.
The Kiwi Ferns have an incident-free set, and kick clear.
The wind is still strong and will play a roll in this match.
History on the side of the Kiwi Ferns
This is the seventh Women's Rugby League World Cup.
New Zealand have made it into the final in EVERY tournament.
They won the first three (2000, 2003, 2008), and have lost the final to Australia in the other three (2013, 2017, 2021).
HT: New Zealand 8 lead Fetu Samoa 0
That is the end of 35 minutes.
New Zealand have two tries and lead 8-0 over Fetu Samoa.
Neither team has been at their best, highlighting how tense a World Cup semifinal is.
34' Kiwi Ferns throw away a great chance
The Kiwi Ferns had a scrum near halfway and could have had a full set to try and get a third try.
But a forward pass on the opening play of the set ended any hopes of a double-digit lead at the break.
Rain is heading for Newcastle
Bit of weather comming down? - Mike
Bit of weather comming down?
The clouds are getting bigger, and look dark.
The wind has also picked up, which will making catching the high ball very tricky.
25' TRY: Stacey Waaka (4) scores for New Zealand
A lovely little chip kick to the in-goal from New Zealand halfback Raecene McGregor landed between two Fetuy Samoa players.
Samoan winger Mercedez Taulelei-Siala needed to attack the footy, but she backed off and let it bounce.
Kiwi Ferns star centre Stacey Waaka charged onto the loose ball and scored.
Meanwhile, the weather is looking ominous.
Thick, dark clouds are heading to Hunter Stadium, and the wind is so strong that the ball would not stay on the kicking tee.
19' Kiwi Ferns hold on the goal line
Terrific defence from New Zealand.
They had to defend four sets on their goal line, and they did it brilliantly.
A big worry for Fetu Samoa as they never really looked like scoring.
18' Fetu Samoa attack, and attack
Fetu Samoa got themselves to the goal line, then shifted left.
The Samoans won a penalty after a player was taken without the footy by New Zealand captain Raecene McGregor.
With another set at the goal line, Fetu Samoa continued to threaten, but the Kiwi Ferns defence was firm.
Fetu Samoa got a third chance when a pass was knocked down by the Kiwi Ferns, and then a fourth set when New Zealand were called offside.
15' Fetu Samoa with a great chance
Fetu Samoa has their best chance of the match, thus far.
Hooker Mary-Jane Taito nailed New Zealand winger Leianne Tufuga and forced the ball loose, giving Fetu Samoa a scrum just 20 metres out.
10' Kiwi Ferns threaten to score
Fetu Samoa needed to scramble to prevent a second try.
Mackenzie Wiki made a run for the right corner and was forced to throw the ball inside.
The ball hung in the air, and if Stacey Waaka could have caught the footy, it would have been a try.
But Waaka was hit as she tried to catch the footy over her head, and Fetus Samoa survived.
5' Samoa force an error, but give the ball straight back
After giving up the first try, Fetu Samoa worked their way back into the contest with strong defence.
The Samoan's forced an error in New Zealand territory and earned a scrum.
But off the scrum, the Samoans dropped the footy and threw away a great chance to get into an attacking position.
2' TRY: Mackenzie Wiki (5) scores for New Zealand
Perfection from the Kiwi Ferns.
With an early chance at Samoa's goal line, the New Zealanders shifted to the right and winger Mackenzie Wiki touched down in the corner — completing the score with a lovely flip.
It was a nice pass from Stacey Waaka, basketball style, to Wiki for the try.
1' Forward pass for Samoa in its first set
Shocking start for Fetus Samoa.
Dummy half Mary-Jane Taito throws a forward pass early in the set.
KICK-OFF: The first women's semifinal is underway
Referee Tara Jones blows her whistle, and we are underway at Hunter Stadium.
New Zealand kick the ball, and Samoa will have the first use of the footy.
Kiwi Ferns with the haka
Fetu Samoa perform the Siva Tau
Kiwi Ferns and Fetu Samoa on the field
Both sets of players have made their way onto Hunter Stadium.
New Zealand has never lost a Rugby League World Cup semifinal in the women's competition.
Fetu Samoa are in their maiden semifinal, a major moment for the women's game.

VALE — Paul Langmack
The rugby league world lost one of it's great people this week.
Paul Langmack, a man who won three premierships with Canterbury in the 1980s, and dedicated so much time in later years to running mental health programs, died this week aged 61.
Team list: Fetu Samoa

Samoa had to make a change after in-form winger Freedom Crichton Ropati suffered an ankle injury last week against England. Anastasia Leatupue (19) comes on to the wing, while Fanua Rimoni starts at lock and Tavarna Papalii moves to the bench.
Despite the underdog status (and a win today would be MASSIVE), Fetu Samoa boasts plenty of talent who have played at the highest level.

Ivana Lolesio knows all about State of Origin with Queensland, Annetta Nuuausala has been in a Test arena for nearly a decade (starting with New Zealand), while players like Destiny Mino-Sinapati (Titans) and Mercedez Taulelei-Siala (Knights) were big reasons their clubs played NRLW finals this season.

Team list: New Zealand Kiwi Ferns
New Zealand are as advertised earlier in the week.
This is a proper side filled with class, and likely the only nation that could realistically challenge the Jillaroos for this year's tite.
Halfback Raecene McGregor is a terrific game-manager, while powerhouse centre Mele Hufanga is a good a ball runner as there is in footy.
Hooker Georgia Hale is a born leader who will organise the team from dummy-half.

Welcome back to the ABC Sport Rugby League World Cup blog
G'day.
Welcome back to ABC Sport's live digital coverage of the 2026 Rugby League World Cup.
We have reached the semifinals, and today, one nation in the men's and women's tournaments will book their spot in next Sunday's final.
In the first women's semifinal, New Zealand faces Samoa, followed by a blockbuster men's semi — New Zealand vs Tonga.
Join us throughout the afternoon and evening as we bring you all of the action from Hunter Stadium in Newcastle.
